title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Volodymyr Mnih, Koray Kavukcuoglu, David Silver, Alex Graves, Ioannis Antonoglou, Daan Wierstra, Martin Riedmiller
abstract: A reinforcement learning agent uses a convolutional network to predict action values from screen pixels and learns control policies across Atari games. Experience replay reuses transitions and reduces correlations between consecutive training examples.

title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
abstract: An amortized variational encoder approximates a latent posterior, while a decoder models how latent variables generate observations. Reparameterizing a random sample makes gradients of the evidence lower bound practical to estimate by backpropagation.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Ian J. Goodfellow, Jean Pouget-Abadie, Mehdi Mirza, Bing Xu, David Warde-Farley, Sherjil Ozair, Aaron Courville, Yoshua Bengio
abstract: A generator transforms noise into synthetic data and a discriminator tries to distinguish synthetic from observed examples. Training both neural networks as competitors provides an implicit generative model that can sample without computing an explicit likelihood.

title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
abstract: Adam updates parameters using running estimates of the mean and uncentered variance of stochastic gradients. Bias correction and coordinate-specific scaling make this optimizer practical for fitting large machine learning models.

title: Attention Is All You Need
authors: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Lukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
abstract: The Transformer stacks multi-head self-attention and feed-forward layers in an encoder and decoder. Its parallel sequence processing improves translation training compared with recurrent architectures and provides a foundation for later language models.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
authors: Jacob Devlin, Ming-Wei Chang, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova
abstract: BERT learns contextual token representations by predicting masked tokens with access to the surrounding text. A pretrained bidirectional Transformer can be fine-tuned for natural language inference, question answering and other language understanding tasks.

title: On the Convergence of Adam and Beyond
authors: Sashank J. Reddi, Satyen Kale, Sanjiv Kumar
abstract: This analysis identifies settings where Adam can fail to converge because its adaptive learning rates discard past gradients too quickly. AMSGrad retains a running maximum of the second moment estimate to address that issue.

title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
authors: Yinhan Liu, Myle Ott, Naman Goyal, Jingfei Du, Mandar Joshi, Danqi Chen, Omer Levy, Mike Lewis, Luke Zettlemoyer, Veselin Stoyanov
abstract: RoBERTa revisits the training recipe for masked language models. Larger datasets and batches, longer training and dynamic masking improve performance without introducing a new Transformer architecture.

title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
abstract: Sentence-BERT trains shared encoders to produce reusable sentence vectors. Comparing those embeddings by cosine similarity makes semantic search and clustering practical without running a language model on every pair of sentences.

title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
authors: Colin Raffel, Noam Shazeer, Adam Roberts, Katherine Lee, Sharan Narang, Michael Matena, Yanqi Zhou, Wei Li, Peter J. Liu
abstract: T5 represents language tasks as text inputs paired with text outputs. This shared format supports experiments on data, pretraining objectives and model scale for translation, summarization and question answering.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: Vladimir Karpukhin, Barlas Oğuz, Sewon Min, Patrick Lewis, Ledell Wu, Sergey Edunov, Danqi Chen, Wen-tau Yih
abstract: Separate neural encoders map a question and a passage into dense vectors. Nearest-neighbor retrieval over precomputed passage vectors supplies candidate evidence to an open-domain question answering system.

title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
abstract: ColBERT encodes query tokens and document tokens independently with BERT, then scores matches using late interaction between contextual token vectors. Precomputing document vectors supports fine-grained passage retrieval.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandra Piktus, Fabio Petroni, Vladimir Karpukhin, Naman Goyal, Heinrich Küttler, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Tim Rocktäschel, Sebastian Riedel, Douwe Kiela
abstract: A retrieval-augmented text generator conditions on evidence from a dense index of Wikipedia passages. The approach gives a sequence-to-sequence model an external source of knowledge for question answering and generation.

title: BEIR: A Heterogenous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
authors: Nandan Thakur, Nils Reimers, Andreas Rücklé, Abhishek Srivastava, Iryna Gurevych
abstract: BEIR collects retrieval tasks across diverse domains to measure generalization without task-specific training. The comparison includes lexical search, dense embeddings and more expensive reranking systems.

title: SPLADE: Sparse Lexical and Expansion Model for First Stage Ranking
authors: Thibault Formal, Benjamin Piwowarski, Stéphane Clinchant
abstract: SPLADE uses a language model to learn sparse term weights and vocabulary expansion for queries and documents. Sparse vectors support fast retrieval through an inverted index while retaining learned associations between terms.
